method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer) 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation' (2025), 24 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12180710). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065) 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)' (2024), 15 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <permissions> element for PMC11385272). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the GETH-TC 2024 consensus on CMV after allogeneic stem cell transplant, paraphrased and hash-anchored, to cover the stem cell transplant setting S1 omits; the S1 claims are unchanged. No Australian or New Zealand CMV guideline was found (Europe PMC: only an ANZTCT practice survey, Intern Med J 2026). The ASTCT 2025 HCT CMV guideline (CC BY-NC-ND) returned a bot challenge at both ScienceDirect and the journal site, and ECIL-7 is paywalled. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S2 Table 1 (the consensus summary: CAR-T and targeted-drug monitoring, doubling time, diagnosis of end-organ disease, stopping pre-emptive therapy, resistance testing, immune monitoring and virus-specific T cells). S1's dosing tables have merged cells and were not extracted.

claims.claim: **Before transplant, test CMV IgG serology in both donor and recipient to stratify risk** (strong, high). Do not use CMV IgM or combined IgG/IgM tests (strong, low).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Equivocal serology:** in adults, treat an equivocal donor as positive, and place an equivocal recipient in the highest applicable risk group for post-transplant decisions (strong, low).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Measure CMV with a quantitative nucleic acid test calibrated to the WHO standard,** for diagnosis, pre-emptive surveillance and treatment monitoring (strong, high). Read changes on a log10 scale, and keep the same specimen type throughout monitoring (strong, high).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CMV retinitis is a clinical diagnosis made on eye examination;** blood CMV DNA rarely predicts it.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Every at-risk recipient needs a prevention plan: universal prophylaxis, or surveillance with pre-emptive therapy** (strong, high). Routine DNAemia monitoring is not needed while on correctly dosed prophylaxis (strong, moderate).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High-risk D+/R– kidney recipients:** prophylaxis (strong, high) or pre-emptive therapy (strong, moderate) are both acceptable; for prophylaxis use valganciclovir, ganciclovir or letermovir (strong, high).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Heart and lung recipients (D+/R– or R+): prophylaxis is suggested over pre-emptive therapy,** as it is linked to less CMV and fewer indirect effects on the graft and survival (weak, low).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prophylaxis length for D+/R–:** kidney 6 months (strong, high); liver, heart and pancreas 3 to 6 months; lung 12 months (strong, moderate), which some experts extend.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prophylaxis length for R+:** 3 months for routine kidney, pancreas, liver and heart recipients; 3 to 6 months with more potent immunosuppression (lymphocyte-depleting antibodies, desensitisation) or intestinal and composite grafts; lung 6–12 months (strong, moderate).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If valganciclovir or ganciclovir prophylaxis is not tolerated, switch to pre-emptive therapy or to letermovir prophylaxis** (weak, low).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pre-emptive strategy:** test CMV at least weekly for 12–16 weeks after transplant (less often raises disease risk), with lower treatment thresholds for D+/R– than R+ (strong, moderate).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **When DNAemia crosses the threshold in a well patient, treat with valganciclovir (strong, high) until it clears, for at least 2 weeks;** IV ganciclovir is less preferred unless absorption is a concern.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With D–/R–, letermovir prophylaxis or a pre-emptive approach, cover other herpesviruses** (varicella, herpes simplex) with aciclovir, famciclovir or valaciclovir (strong, high). Use leukoreduced or CMV-seronegative blood, especially for D–/R– (strong, moderate).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low-dose valganciclovir prophylaxis is not recommended** (weak, low).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rejection treated with lymphocyte-depleting antibodies should restart prophylaxis or pre-emptive therapy for 4–12 weeks** (weak, moderate).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First-line treatment with normal kidney function: oral valganciclovir 900 mg or IV ganciclovir 5 mg/kg, each 12-hourly** (strong, moderate). Oral for mild to moderate disease if the patient can take and keep it down; IV for severe or life-threatening disease, stepping down to oral once improving.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral ganciclovir, aciclovir and valaciclovir are not treatments for CMV disease** (strong, moderate); letermovir monotherapy lacks evidence and resistance develops easily.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not change drugs in the first 2 weeks if the patient is improving clinically,** even if DNAemia is flat or rising, as it often rises in week one. Suspect resistance after more than 4 weeks' cumulative antiviral exposure with failure despite at least 2 weeks of proper dosing.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor weekly DNAemia and kidney function (Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance, not eGFR) during treatment.** Reduce doses only for worsening kidney function, not for leukopenia alone; for leukopenia, consider G-CSF or adjust other marrow-suppressing drugs.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat for at least 2 weeks and until the disease has resolved and DNAemia is below the laboratory's threshold** (strong, moderate). Secondary prophylaxis is not routine but may be used in high-risk situations, typically for 8–12 weeks.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without concurrent rejection, consider reducing immunosuppression** in severe disease, poor response, high viral load or cytopenia (weak, very low).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If valganciclovir or ganciclovir is not tolerated, use maribavir or foscarnet second-line** (strong, low), chosen on viral load, nephrotoxicity risk and severity.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor CMV DNA at least weekly in every allogeneic stem cell transplant recipient from within the first two weeks to day +100, whatever the serostatus** (AII). Continue at that frequency until immunosuppression stops in high-risk patients: cord blood grafts, pre-emptive therapy before day 100, letermovir beyond day 100, moderate to severe GVHD or high-dose steroids.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **CAR-T cells and targeted drugs:** in high-risk patients, check CMV DNA before CAR-T infusion and keep checking until day 60 or until blood counts recover. Patients on BTK or JAK inhibitors do not need routine checks unless there is a clinical reason.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Letermovir prophylaxis is the one agent shown to cut clinically significant CMV and all-cause mortality,** with top-grade (A-I) recommendations in guidelines. If it cannot be given to everyone, target higher-risk grafts (BII): seropositive recipient with a seronegative donor, HLA mismatch at A, B or DR, post-transplant cyclophosphamide, cord blood, or ex vivo T-cell depletion.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Continue letermovir to day +100 in all eligible patients, and to at least day +200 during active GVHD treated with steroids above 0.5 mg/kg/day** (AI).
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **DNAemia on letermovir is often abortive** (fragmented DNA that clears without treatment), so keep weekly monitoring but start pre-emptive therapy only at a higher level, for example 1,500 IU/mL in plasma or 10,000 IU/mL in whole blood (BII). Do not treat a single isolated positive result; confirm true replication before resistance testing.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Without prophylaxis, pre-emptive thresholds of 2–3 log10 IU/mL gave similar protection from CMV disease** (BIIr); each centre should set its own threshold for its assay and sample type. Pre-emptive therapy stays the strategy where universal letermovir is not feasible and after letermovir failure.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **A viral load that doubles in 2 days or less supports starting pre-emptive therapy,** particularly where the centre's threshold is 1,500 IU/mL (S2 summary table).
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **A blood CMV DNA level cannot by itself diagnose CMV pneumonia or gut disease;** tissue histopathology and virological evidence from the organ are needed.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pre-emptive drugs:** IV ganciclovir (AI) or oral valganciclovir, limited by marrow and kidney toxicity; foscarnet works as well (AI) and is preferred with neutropenia or thrombocytopenia. Maribavir 400 mg twice daily cleared viraemia comparably with fewer neutropenia stops, so it is an alternative when neutropenia develops (BI).
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Stop pre-emptive therapy once PCR is negative after at least 15 days,** as ECIL and ASTCT advise (the consensus agrees, AII).
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **S2's summary table states the stopping rule more loosely:** consider ending pre-emptive therapy at the first negative PCR, which limits drug toxicity without raising recurrence.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Recurrent DNAemia:** letermovir secondary prophylaxis may be the choice if there is no letermovir-resistance mutation and DNAemia is negative before starting (BII).
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Refractory or resistant infection after stem cell transplant:** foscarnet (AIIu), or cidofovir 5 mg/kg weekly if kidney function allows (BIIu); oral maribavir 400 mg every 12 hours is becoming standard, especially with blood or kidney toxicity (AI). Half-dose ganciclovir plus foscarnet is a second- or third-line option (CIIu); reduce immunosuppression, including steroids, if there is no active GVHD (BIII). Letermovir is not a rescue drug.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **When to test for resistance after stem cell transplant (S2 summary table):** send mutational analysis if DNAemia has not cleared after 3 weeks of properly dosed antiviral therapy, or if it rises after 2 weeks; confirm resistance with genotypic and phenotypic methods.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Virus-specific T cells** (adoptive transfer) can be considered, refractory infection included. Routine immune monitoring is not yet standard, but S2 asks centres to measure CMV immunity where they can, to build real-world evidence.
claims.locator: Piñana JL, Giménez E, Vázquez L, Marcos MÁ, et al., Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC), Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis 16(1):e2024065 (doi 10.4084/MJHID.2024.065), 'Update on Cytomegalovirus Infection Management in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients. A Consensus Document of the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cell Therapy (GETH-TC)', 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385272/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Genotype for resistance after at least 4 weeks of antiviral exposure with a refractory viral-load response after at least 2 weeks of optimal dosing** (strong, high), on a sample whose viral load exceeds 1000 IU/mL (3 log10), so the mutation read-out is reliable.
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maribavir is the main alternative for ganciclovir- or foscarnet-resistant CMV** (strong, high). Foscarnet is suggested first in a clinically unwell patient with a high viral load and suspected or proven ganciclovir resistance (weak, low).
claims.locator: The Transplantation Society International CMV Consensus Group (Kotton, Kumar, Humar et al.), Transplantation (Wolters Kluwer), 'The Fourth International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid Organ Transplantation', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12180710/, retrieved 2026-09-23
